content.value_statement: New Expo projects can lack a consistent structure and core development tooling. This skill provides a staged setup guide for TypeScript, SQLite, state management, testing, linting, and project checks.
actual_capabilities: Installs and initializes TypeScript for a React Native and Expo project.
Creates a feature-oriented source directory structure.
Sets up an Expo SQLite database client with Drizzle ORM.
Adds a basic Zustand application store example.
Configures Jest testing and npm scripts for common development tasks.
Provides checks for compilation, testing, linting, database access, and app platforms.
limitations: It is a setup guide and does not run commands or inspect an existing project automatically.
It targets React Native projects that use Expo, not web-only or native-only applications.
It provides starter configuration and does not design feature-specific data models or screens.
Package versions and Expo SDK compatibility require confirmation in the target project.

use_cases.title: Start a mobile application
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable foundation for a new Expo application before feature development begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize team project setup
use_cases.description: Use the staged checklist to align a team on folders, scripts, testing, and quality checks.

use_cases.title: Add core tooling to a prototype
use_cases.description: Add TypeScript, local storage, state management, and tests to an existing Expo prototype.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a basic Expo foundation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this guide to plan a basic Expo project setup with TypeScript, a source directory structure, and verification steps. Ask before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Add local data storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the SQLite and Drizzle portions of this guide to my Expo app. List the dependencies, files, and migration steps before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure team quality tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this guide to add Jest, ESLint, Prettier, and package scripts to my Expo project. Preserve my existing scripts and explain each proposed change.

prompt_templates.title: Review architecture readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my Expo project against this setup guide. Identify missing foundations, dependency compatibility concerns, and a safe incremental implementation plan.

output_examples.input: Plan a new Expo application foundation with TypeScript and testing.
output: A staged installation order for TypeScript and test dependencies.
A proposed source folder layout for application, feature, shared, database, and theme code.
A verification checklist for type checks, tests, linting, and mobile platforms.

output_examples.input: Add a local database to an Expo prototype.
output: The Expo SQLite and Drizzle dependencies to add.
A database client location and migration folder structure.
Steps to validate that local queries work after setup.

best_practices: Install and validate one subsystem before adding the next subsystem.
Check package compatibility with the Expo SDK before installing dependencies.
Commit each successful setup stage so changes are easy to review and revert.
anti_patterns: Do not install every dependency before confirming the project requirements.
Do not overwrite existing configuration files without reviewing their current settings.
Do not assume package commands or versions are compatible with every Expo SDK release.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports React Native applications that use Expo.

faq.question: Does this skill execute installation commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and guidance for an agent or developer to review and run.

faq.question: Can I use it with an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. Review existing configuration first and add each missing subsystem incrementally.

faq.question: Which database approach does it describe?
faq.answer: It describes Expo SQLite with Drizzle ORM and a migrations directory.

faq.question: Does it configure production deployment?
faq.answer: No. It covers local project foundations, not release pipelines or store deployment.

faq.question: Should I use the listed package versions directly?
faq.answer: Confirm package versions against your Expo SDK and existing dependencies before installation.
